comment.narrative: One 5day ToT with 10 participants producing a cadre of trainers capable of teaching the Countering Hate Speech and AntiDisinformation Toolkit to other journalists.

Session 1 9Session 2 8Session 3 5Session 4 6Session 5 6Internews organized five training sessions on factchecking verification and antidisinformation and countering hate speech. The training comprised of five sessions on forms and magnitude of misdisinformation techniques to identify them introduction to factchecking and tools used to carry out factchecks how to write a factchecked story and a practical session to practice. Digital hygiene fundamentals evaluating photos and videos responding appropriately to misinformation and authenticating reports from social media and the internet were the main topics of the course. Initially the plan was to train 10 journalists however due to competing priorities only nine attended all the sessions. As all the participants were not able to attend the full sessions therefore to ensure all participants received the full training sessions were recorded and shared with participants following each session.

The factchecked stories published through these incubators served as constant checkups on the government and bureaucracy with 57 of the total stories published covering and debunking reports around politics and bureaucracy followed by 15 of them around international relations with respect to the Maldives. With some of the best performing stories published through these incubators uncovering some of the most hardhitting political and bureaucratic themes. Some of the top performing stories are listed below for context1.Fraud and deception the truth about the investor for Thinadhoo airport an expose on the Maldivian government inept launch of a new airport which was signed with fraudulent contractor having ties with Maldivian government officials.2.Company awarded Laamu projects blacklisted by banks again an expose on how the Maldivian government awarded the contract to redevelop the Kadhdhoo airport to a Chinese company which is backlisted by World Bank for fraudulent activities. 3.Kuwait grant aid for school building in Khaleels personal account a story on how the grant provided by the Kuwait Fund to build a school was siphoned into the Health Ministers personal bank account. These stories published through media outlets empowered by PFEM projects shows that how the project has enabled its beneficiaries to uphold bastions of accountability by building their capacities on publishing a factchecked story.
